summary: Decide whether and where GPU acceleration helps a complete workload, including launch and transfer costs.
outcomes: Estimate an acceleration break-even point from measured costs.
Partition a pipeline while preserving data residency and semantics.
sequence: Trace a CPU baseline from input to result.
Separate serial work, parallel work, transfer and launch costs.
Calculate fixed-size speedup and a simple break-even case.
Batch work and keep intermediates resident where appropriate.
Compare latency, throughput, cost and developer effort.

visual.question: When does a faster kernel make the whole application slower?
visual.interaction: Vary input size and transfer reuse; compare full runtimes.

practice.task: Choose CPU, library GPU or custom GPU execution for three workloads.
practice.success: Decision includes end-to-end measurements and a defensible break-even estimate.
